# Cohort 106: shared managed conversation turn publication

Approved #2542/#2151 original selected construction and mutation/raw_sql_policy govern.
The existing managed turn fixture remains the live lifecycle/session/claim/completion
owner; its shared conformance caller no longer receives a pool/dialect or reconstructs
a raw event transaction. The exact trigger is constructed explicitly and persisted
through existing CommitSemanticEvent on the original selected owner.

Exact UUID, existing run, external conformance producer, empty task/payload/envelope,
live mode, current creation clock and NoRoutingSource are preserved. In particular,
the convenience event constructor's default root routing source is NOT substituted
for the old absent source. Canonical publication now supplies its coupled scope/facts
instead of retaining the partial record-only producer. This is fixture setup, not a
claim of public operator publication admission; no production semantics are changed.

All three public readback consumers now use native PostgreSQL construction: canonical
turn summary, audit rows never becoming live sessions, and runtime-log turn blocks
omitted from public conversation projections. Their turn payloads, parse/latency,
messages/summary/outcome/activity/privacy/live-versus-audit assertions remain unchanged.
The helper preserves the full existing ManagedAgentTurnFixture fields and original
selected store on both Store and Selected; publication requires real original writes
and zero active work before managed completion begins. No new owner/port/SQL is added.

Four finite recipes/type overlay cover the helper and all consumers. Hostile source,
event/session/owner/receipt substitutions are rejected. Focused race proof runs all
three actual PostgreSQL public projection roots; native managed-turn selected-owner
controls on both stores are cited separately. The original raw/dialect helper imports
and pool-forwarding callers are deleted, not preserved behind another alias.

Value: canonical event setup preceding actual lifecycle-authorized managed completion,
shared native construction and elimination of the synthetic record transaction path.
No measured flake-rate improvement is claimed. Existing architecture/watchlist applies;
no framework/compatibility/new issue. Parent remaining raw/getter/protocol debt and
zero-debt/strict guards/SQLite fork deadline/final qualification remain open.
